target.title: fix(sdk): preserve zero event id components
target.body:
Closes #101768

AI-assisted: drafted and validated by Codex. I understand the change: it preserves protocol-valid zero values when the SDK builds normalized event ids.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where SDK consumers could receive normalized gateway event ids that silently dropped valid `seq: 0` and `ts: 0` components, weakening replay/live dedupe identity for zero-sequence gateway events.

## Why This Change Was Made

The gateway protocol allows event sequence values starting at zero, but `normalizeGatewayEvent()` built ids with a truthy filter. This change filters out only absent optional parts, so numeric zero values remain part of the stable SDK event id.

## User Impact

SDK consumers now get stable normalized ids for the first gateway event in a stream, avoiding avoidable replay or dedupe confusion around valid zero-valued sequence and timestamp fields.

## Evidence

- Focused proof passed: `/Users/harjothk/.cache/codex-runtimes/codex-primary-runtime/dependencies/node/bin/node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/sdk/src/normalize.test.ts -- --reporter=verbose` (1 file, 5 tests).
